items.reason: Artifacts assigns exploration its own type and orders it between spec and progress.
Dashboard artifacts consume the same ordered artifact list.
The orphan check explicitly exempts ExplorationFileName.
Other manifest validation and orphan rejection remain intact.
ExploreRequested reads the set-level explore boolean.
Missing or false explore values disable automatic exploration.
ExplorerOverride parses the shared AgentDirective shape.
The guide explicitly distinguishes exploration’s opt-in from verify/refine’s opt-out.
The guide states the shared-seam and dependent-later-task rule.
Shared constants generate the guide, with a manifest-loading consistency test.
The command launches an Explorer with the task listing, task bodies and optional spec.
The prompt requests locations, ownership, invariants, test shape and ranged reads.
The prompt requires path-or-symbol claims, approximately one page and the observed tree.
The requested report structure contains no prior-art section.
Successful passes atomically replace the flat exploration.md file.
Explore has its own captured-run phase, spend accounting and retry-cap attribution.
Manual exploration bypasses both participation and automatic-exploration gates.
Failed, timed-out and interrupted runs return without replacing the report.
The command test drives agent output through report creation and captured-run replay.
Both implementation entry points conditionally include the report path and explanation.
Implementation prompts receive only the report path, with a long-body exclusion test.
The prompt limits edits to lines this attempt falsified.
The edit boundary explicitly permits the exploration report beside the task file.
The prior-art block remains unchanged, with comparison coverage.
Assist includes the exploration pointer beside refinement and recent progress.
Implement and assist goldens cover report-present and report-absent cases.
The drain invokes exploration before executing its first selected task.
An existing report bypasses the Explorer and its spending.
Undeclared sets bypass automatic exploration.
The dedicated work.explore gate defaults on when its group or key is absent.
Disabling the machine gate suppresses automatic passes without disabling manual exploration.
Resolution applies CLI overrides before manifest directives, configuration and defaults.
HumanCompleted explicitly bypasses the automatic explore phase.
Existing reports are reused without comparing their recorded tree to the checkout.
Whole-drain tests assert exploration runs without a report and skips with one.
The shared fallback walker applies the standard retry cap and delays.
Exhausted exploration without a report derives EXPLORE-FAILED and stops the drain.
Parking derives from captured-run metadata and report absence without schema changes.
EXPLORE-FAILED is separate from the unchanged BLOCKED status.
Daemon and automatic READY selection exclude EXPLORE-FAILED rows.
attendableHITLTaskSets ignores row status, so a parked set with an eligible HITL task remains selectable.
A failed manual explore can derive a park without a progress record; only the drain phase appends one.
--skip-explore bypasses both automatic exploration and the existing park for that drain.
Writing a report or retracting explore clears the derived park.
CONTEXT.md lists EXPLORE-FAILED among drain stops and automatic-selection exclusions.
Unexplored sets carry separate mark and reason fields.
Undeclared sets receive no exploration mark.
Refresh resolves exploration once into fields shared by the four requested surfaces.
Shared status segments render parked sets’ exploration marks on dashboard rows and work status.
Reports on undeclared sets lack the path-and-tree detail pointer because ResolveExploreMark returns before reading them.
The sign-off gate omits existing exploration reports when explore is absent or false.
After report deletion, a completed captured run falls through to the failed reason, parking instead of re-exploring.

scores.rationale: Good reuse and broad tests, but recovery, HITL selection, progress recording and manually generated report visibility have correctness gaps.
